docs.title: Welcome to letterboxdpy
docs.text: A modern, fast, and feature-rich Python library for scraping and interacting with Letterboxd data.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Core Letterboxd Entities: First-class support for User, Movie, Search, List, and Films.
  • WAF & Cloudflare Resilient: Built with curl_cffi using modern browser impersonation (chrome120) and RFC-compliant URL normalization.
  • Deep User Insights: Extract watchlists, diary logs, likes, reviews, followers, following, and genre distribution.
  • Advanced Film Discovery: Discover films by genre, sub-genre, themes, release years, decades, or streaming services.
  • Type Annotated & Clean: Clean, structured return models with consistent snake_case keys and ISO 8601 timestamps.

docs.title: Development Guide
docs.text: This guide covers setting up your development environment, running tests, linting, building documentation, and contributing to letterboxdpy.

docs.title: Environment Setup
docs.text:
letterboxdpy requires Python 3.10 or higher.

Clone the repository and install all optional development dependencies:

git clone https://github.com/nmcassa/letterboxdpy.git
cd letterboxdpy

# Install in editable mode with development, docs, and example dependencies
pip install -e ".[dev,docs,examples]"

docs.title: Code Quality & Linting
docs.text:
This project uses Ruff for fast Python linting and formatting.

# Check for lint issues
ruff check .

# Automatically fix fixable issues
ruff check --fix .

# Format code
ruff format .

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: The test suite separates fast, deterministic offline unit tests from live external network tests against Letterboxd (marked as smoke).

docs.title: Run Offline Unit Tests (Default)
docs.text:
Executes parser and model tests in ~0.5 seconds without any external network calls:

python -m pytest

docs.title: Run Live Network Tests (Smoke Marker)
docs.text:
Executes integration tests directly against live Letterboxd endpoints:

python -m pytest -m smoke

docs.title: Run All Tests
docs.text:
python -m pytest -m "smoke or not smoke"

[!NOTE] Tests that require an authenticated Letterboxd session (e.g. test_auth.py) are automatically skipped if no valid .cookie file is present. This ensures the suite runs cleanly in CI environments without credentials.

mkdocs build --strict

docs.title: Pre-commit Hooks
docs.text:
Pre-commit hooks automatically check linting rules with Ruff and validate commit title length before each commit:

  • Ruff & Ruff-Format: Runs on commit to verify and auto-format staged files.
  • Commit Title Length: Validates that the first line of the commit message follows Conventional Commits and is at or under 62 characters (checked on commit-msg).
# Install hooks for both pre-commit and commit-msg stages
pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type commit-msg

# Run manually against all files
pre-commit run --all-files

docs.title: CI / CD Pipeline
docs.text:
GitHub Actions automatically runs on every push and pull request against the main branch:

  1. Lint & Test: Validates formatting with Ruff and executes the pytest offline test suite across all supported Python versions (3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14).
  2. Verify Docs: Runs mkdocs build --strict to ensure zero broken links or documentation errors.
  3. Deploy Docs: Builds and deploys the site to GitHub Pages on every push to main.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide walks you through installing letterboxdpy and making your first queries.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, or 3.14
  • Active internet connection (Letterboxd requests are sent over HTTPS)

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install the package via pip:

pip install letterboxdpy

If you plan to run the included examples (which use matplotlib, rich, pillow, etc.):

pip install "letterboxdpy[examples]"

docs.title: Cloudflare & Network Resilience
docs.text:
Letterboxd is protected by Cloudflare WAF. letterboxdpy includes built-in safeguards to ensure reliable data retrieval:

  1. Browser Impersonation: Uses curl_cffi to mimic real browser TLS fingerprints (chrome120).
  2. Canonical URL Normalization: Automatically validates and appends canonical trailing slashes (/) per Letterboxd routing standards, preventing 403 challenge blocks and redundant redirects.
  3. Retry Strategy: Automatically retries transient network interruptions with progressive backoff timeouts.

docs.title: letterboxdpy.utils.utils_url.normalize_letterboxd_url(url)
docs.text: Normalizes Letterboxd URLs to ensure canonical trailing slashes. Prevents Cloudflare WAF challenges and redundant 301/302 redirects. Preserves query parameters, fragments, and avoids file extensions.

docs.title: letterboxdpy.utils.utils_url.get_page_url(base_url, page, params='')
docs.text:
Generate a paginated URL from a base URL and page number. Ensures no double slashes and consistent trailing slashes.

Note

Letterboxd accepts both '/page/1/' and the clean root URL '/', but canonical pagination links on Letterboxd point to the root path for page 1, while page 2+ follow '/page/{N}/'.

docs.title: Authentication & Settings Guide
docs.text: The letterboxdpy.auth and letterboxdpy.account.settings modules enable secure authenticated interactions with Letterboxd for managing profile data, personal settings, and private actions.

docs.title: Session Architecture
docs.text:
UserSession is trace-locked: every behavior matches legitimate browser traffic with automated CSRF extraction and token management.

Sessions are stored locally in JSON format at .cookie/session.json by default (with strict permissions chmod 600 on POSIX systems).

sequenceDiagram
    participant App as Application Code
    participant Session as UserSession
    participant Scraper as Global Scraper
    participant LB as Letterboxd Server

    App->>Session: UserSession.ensure()
    alt Session File Exists & Valid
        Session->>LB: Validate session cookie
        LB-->>Session: 200 OK (Authenticated)
    else Missing or Expired Session
        Session->>LB: GET /sign-in/ (Extract CSRF)
        LB-->>Session: Form + CSRF Token
        Session->>LB: POST /user/login.do
        LB-->>Session: Session Cookies
        Session->>Session: Persist to .cookie/session.json
    end
    Session->>Scraper: Synchronize cookies & CSRF
    App->>LB: Authenticated Requests

docs.title: Automatic Session Initialization
docs.text:
Use UserSession.ensure() to seamlessly use an existing session or prompt for login interactively if unauthenticated:

from letterboxdpy.auth import UserSession

# Loads existing session or initiates login
session = UserSession.ensure()
print(f"Authenticated as: {session.username}")

docs.title: Programmatic Login
docs.text:
from letterboxdpy.auth import UserSession

session = UserSession.login("your_username", "your_password")

docs.title: Loading from Custom Storage
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from letterboxdpy.auth import UserSession

session = UserSession.load(Path(".cookie/session.json"))

docs.title: Managing Profile & Settings
docs.text:
Once authenticated, use UserSettings to inspect or update account configurations:

from letterboxdpy.auth import UserSession
from letterboxdpy.account.settings import UserSettings

session = UserSession.ensure()
settings = UserSettings(session)

# 1. Fetch current profile
profile = settings.get_profile()
print(f"Bio: {profile.get('bio')}")
print(f"Location: {profile.get('location')}")

# 2. Update profile details
settings.update_profile({
    "location": "New York, USA",
    "website": "https://example.com",
    "bio": "Cinephile and Python enthusiast."
})

# 3. Notification preferences
notifs = settings.get_notifications()
settings.update_notifications({
    "emailEditorial": True,
    "pushFollowers": False
})

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text: [!WARNING] Keep your .cookie/ directory private. Never commit session files to version control repositories. Ensure .cookie/ is present in your .gitignore.

docs.title: Films & Discovery Guide
docs.text: letterboxdpy provides discovery functions to explore films on Letterboxd by streaming service, release year, decade, genres, and curated themes.

from letterboxdpy.films import (
    get_movies_by_genre,

horror_films = get_movies_by_genre("horror", max=10)

# 2. By Theme
epic_heroes = get_movies_by_theme("epic-heroes", max=5)

# 3. By Mini-Theme
democracy_films = get_movies_by_mini_theme(
    "politician-assassination-democracy-president-compelling", 
    max=5
)

# 4. Upcoming releases
upcoming = get_upcoming_movies(max=5)

docs.title: List Guide
docs.text: The List class allows extracting metadata, film entries, authors, and notes from any user-curated Letterboxd list.

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
from letterboxdpy.list import List

# Initialize with author username and list slug
film_list = List("nmcassa", "movies-to-watch-with-priscilla-park")

print(f"Title: {film_list.title}")
print(f"Author: {film_list.author}")
print(f"Total Films: {film_list.count}")
print(f"Description: {film_list.description}")

docs.title: Iterating Over Movies
docs.text:
A List instance can be iterated or accessed like a collection:

# Number of films
total = len(film_list)

# Access all movies dictionary
for slug, movie in film_list.movies.items():
    print(f"- {movie['name']} ({movie['year']}) -> {movie['url']}")

docs.title: List Metadata
docs.text:
Available properties on a List instance:

  • film_list.list_id: Unique numeric Letterboxd list ID
  • film_list.title: List title
  • film_list.author: List creator's username
  • film_list.url: Canonical Letterboxd URL
  • film_list.count: Total count of films in the list
  • film_list.date_created: Creation timestamp (ISO 8601)
  • film_list.date_updated: Last modified timestamp (ISO 8601)
  • film_list.description: Full text description / list notes
  • film_list.tags: List of tags assigned to the list

docs.title: Movie Guide

docs.title: Filtering Results
docs.text:
Use the SearchFilter enum or strings to narrow down your query:

# Search exclusively for films
film_search = Search("Dune", search_filter=SearchFilter.FILMS)

# Search for members/users
member_search = Search("nmcassa", search_filter=SearchFilter.MEMBERS)

# Search for user lists
list_search = Search("Cyberpunk", search_filter=SearchFilter.LISTS)

# Search for reviews
review_search = Search("Oppenheimer", search_filter=SearchFilter.REVIEWS)

docs.title: Watchlist Guide
docs.text: The Watchlist class provides tools to inspect and extract a user's saved watchlist, with support for advanced Letterboxd filters.

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
from letterboxdpy.watchlist import Watchlist

watchlist = Watchlist("nmcassa")
watchlist.movies # lazy load

print(f"Total Watchlist Films: {watchlist.count}")
for movie_id, film in list(watchlist.movies.items())[:5]:
    print(f"- {film['name']} ({film['year']})")
Example Watchlist Payload Structure 
{
  "username": "nmcassa",
  "url": "https://letterboxd.com/nmcassa/watchlist",
  "count": 134,
  "movies": {
    "51315": {
      "slug": "videodrome",

docs.title: Filtering Watchlists
docs.text:
Letterboxd supports rich URL-based filters on watchlists. You can pass filter dictionaries directly when using the user page handler:

Filter by GenreFilter by Decade / YearFilter by Streaming Service 
# Positive genre filter
mystery_watchlist = user.pages.watchlist.get_watchlist(
    filters={"genre": ["mystery"]}
)

# Negative genre filter (exclude action)
no_action = user.pages.watchlist.get_watchlist(
    filters={"genre": ["-action"]}
)

# 1990s films in watchlist
nineties = user.pages.watchlist.get_watchlist(
    filters={"decade": "1990s"}
)

# Released in 2023
released_2023 = user.pages.watchlist.get_watchlist(
    filters={"year": "2023"}
)

# Available on Criterion Channel or Netflix
streaming = user.pages.watchlist.get_watchlist(
    filters={"service": ["criterion-channel"]}
)
